title: The Apollo 11 Code That Saved Astronauts From Total Crash — Engineering Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Prioritizing critical tasks via asynchronous executive scheduling under resource constraints.
summary: The Apollo Guidance Computer (AGC) software utilized a real-time executive to manage task preemption, ensuring mission-critical navigation kept priority during hardware overload. It serves as the foundational case study for robust error handling and fail-safe recovery in embedded real-time systems.

key_concepts.name: Executive Priority Scheduling
key_concepts.detail: The 'Exec' program implemented a preemptive priority-based scheduler using 'job queues' to ensure critical guidance tasks interrupted non-essential telemetry tasks during CPU saturation events.

key_concepts.name: Restart Protection
key_concepts.detail: The system employed a soft-restart mechanism that cleared non-essential volatile memory while preserving critical state vectors, allowing the computer to recover navigation within seconds of an overflow.

key_concepts.name: Hardware/Software Handshaking
key_concepts.detail: The 1201/1202 alarms were triggered by hardware interrupts exceeding the cyclic executive's cycle time, forcing the software to purge low-priority tasks and resume high-priority guidance loops.

code_cheatsheet.explanation: Simulates monitoring process priorities in real-time to identify bottlenecks causing potential system hangs or CPU saturation.
Demonstrates a basic architectural pattern for fault-tolerant task execution, mirroring the AGC's philosophy of isolating critical loops from failure-prone sub-tasks.

best_practices: Design for graceful degradation: Identify non-essential tasks that can be dropped during high-load scenarios.
Implement asynchronous state isolation: Separate critical control logic from I/O or background telemetry processing.
Utilize watchdog timers or software supervisors: Always maintain an external mechanism to reset the system state without total power cycling.
Fail fast, recover faster: Prioritize system uptime through state preservation rather than attempting total execution completion.

interview_qa.question: How do you handle a system overload where CPU interrupts are exceeding process capability?
interview_qa.answer: Implement an event-driven scheduler that utilizes preemptive priority levels. By categorizing tasks by criticality and purging lower-level tasks when interrupts hit a threshold, the system preserves mission-critical continuity while discarding non-essential telemetry.
